title: A trip to Mindoro Island with Lieutenant MacLauren
summary: A black lieutenant with a Ph.D. takes the show by yacht to Mindoro, where they wade ashore to a tree-house village and relax with the chief's whiskey.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: And I ran into a fellow there, his name was MacLauren, from Oklahoma. He had his Ph.D. in economics. And he was a first lieutenant, black fellow. And he was in the
"Pillars,

Special Service. And he asked me, he said, would you fellows like to go to the island -- we have a little island out there called Mendora. Mendora Island." So we said, "Yes, yes." So one day, we got on this little yacht. There was a yacht -- evidently it belonged to some rich person, you know, they had loaned it to the Army, to use it during the wars. And they had a skipper on it and whatnot, and we took our group up to Mendora Island.

And when we got there, the boat was about 60 feet anchored out from the shore. And we had to get out and pull our trousers up and wade into this island. It was all white sand, a beautiful island. And most of the natives there, they lived up in the trees. They had houses built up in the trees. And they raised corn there, and plenty of coconuts on the island.

And the chief of the group, he had enough whisky up there to float a battleship. MacLauren had been there before and he knew it, see. I think he gave MacLauren a fifth of Old Taylor whisky, I think he did. And we sat on the beach there, with the girls we had in the show, everybody, and we had a ball.
That evening, a little bit later on, we got back on the boat, and went on back in. Which was a great experience for us.
Really was. Had beautiful blue water,
though.
Huh?
Just a beautiful sight -- and the seabed just as clear as I don't know what.
Clear.
Uh-huh.
Clear.
I dove off the boat.
You did?
Uh-huh. Got [Tony], said, 'Look here, it's not too deep there.'
Did you?
Yeah. I think, me and Pruitt.
And the trombone player, what's his name?
Oh, yeah, Weston.
Eddie Kenny Weston, Eddie Kenny Weston.
Eddie Kenny Weston.
Yeah, he --
(Unintelligible) What's his little boy in stir now?
Oh, yeah, yeah. He should be out by now, shouldn't he?
I thought he had a life sentence.
Well, you know, a (Unintelligible) life sentence, that
means that --
Scottie.
Scottie. On good behavior. You can get out on good behavior.
Yeah.
